page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 24 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, paired with 93.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 3.88 GB per core. The instance includes a dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture with 16 GB of VRAM. It does not include local storage, and network connectivity is rated at an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data reveals a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core or GPU-accelerated workloads. Single-core performance is weak, with Geekbench single-core scoring 935.0 and stress-ng single-core CPU performance falling in the bottom 25%. Conversely, multi-core operations, such as Geekbench multi-core at 7397.0 and stress-ng multi-core at 17719.21, achieve average tier results. The hardware excels in LLM inference prompt processing, reaching top-tier status with 8377.38 tokens per second for a small 135M model and 1130.26 tokens per second for a medium 7B model. Text generation on the medium 7B model is also strong at 33.05 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a balanced entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without the premium cost of high-end accelerator classes. However, users must accept tradeoffs: single-threaded CPU tasks and memory performance are weak, and the lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment. This server is suited for workloads that leverage GPU acceleration and multi-threaded CPU execution, such as small-to-medium LLM inference, ray tracing, image processing, and parallelized data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is an x86_64 GPU-accelerated server featuring 24 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 CPU cores at 2.5 GHz, 93.0 GB of RAM, and a single NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. It lacks local storage and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks indicate weak single-core CPU and memory performance, but average multi-core capabilities and top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing, reaching 1130.26 tokens per second on a 7B model. Qualitatively, the server represents a cost-effective option for entry-level GPU workloads, trading off single-threaded speed for parallel processing power. It is best suited for medium-scale LLM inference, image processing, ray tracing, and multi-threaded compute tasks.
